Swiggy has appointed former Myntra Chief Executive Officer Nandita Sinha as the Chief Executive Officer of its quick commerce business Instamart, effective August 3, as the company looks to strengthen leadership amid intensifying competition in the fast-growing quick commerce segment.
...
Sinha succeeds Amitesh Jha, who led Instamart through a key phase of expansion and product innovation. Swiggy did not disclose Jha’s next role.
...
The leadership change also follows a series of senior-level exits across Swiggy and Instamart over the past year as the company reshapes its leadership team. In 2026, several executives have moved on, including Instamart CEO Amitesh Jha. The company has simultaneously brought in external leaders to strengthen businesses across quick commerce and its core food delivery operations, with Sinha’s appointment marking one of its most significant leadership hires this year.

results.title: Swiggy Instamart CEO Amitesh Kumar Jha resigns; Myntra's Nandita Sinha to take charge - The Times of India
results.author: Edited by:  Trisha Mahajan  / TIMESOFINDIA.COM /   Jul 28, 2026, 16:06 IST
highlights:
NEW DELHI: Swiggy-owned quick commerce platform Instamart will have a new chief executive, with Nandita Sinha set to take over as CEO from August 3, following the resignation of Amitesh Kumar Jha.The leadership change was disclosed in a regulatory filing on Tuesday. Jha has stepped down to pursue opportunities outside the company."I hereby tender my resignation from the position of CEO-Instamart, to pursue opportunities outside the organisation," Jha said in his resignation letter addressed to Swiggy Managing Director and Group CEO Sriharsha Majety," as quoted by PTI.Further, hailing his time in the firm, he added on LinkedIn, "When I transitioned from Flipkart to Instamart, the quick-commerce industry was obsessed with one thing: growth at all costs. The prevailing narrative was that rapid delivery was a cash burning machine, and the market was highly skeptical that unit economics could ever work in a hyper competitive space. My mandate was to prove that assumption wrong. Today, as I announce my decision to turn a page and think about the next stage, I am incredibly proud to say we delivered exactly what we set out to build."Also talking about scaling business, Jha said, "Over the last few years, we didn’t just scale Instamart; we fundamentally re-designed how quick commerce operates.
...
By applying deep e-commerce operational rigor to the instant delivery model, we ignored the industry noise and focused entirely on the fundamentals: optimizing the supply chain, making assortment the king, building a highly efficient dark-store network, and obsessing over unit economics."Meanwhile, Sinha joins Instamart from fashion e-commerce platform Myntra, where she served as CEO."Instamart sits at the heart of how India shops for its everyday needs, and I look forward to working with our colleagues, partners and consumers to shape its next chapter of growth," Sinha said.
